title: The Deep Border
premise: Dominic Voss, a former intelligence analyst turned whistle-blower, has lived under four identities since exposing a covert program called LANTERN that he believes killed his partner. When a woman named Ilse returns a debt from a night Dominic has no memory of — a night in Tallinn that never appears in any of his records — she drags him back into the world he fled. Together they uncover a plot to sabotage the Baltic Sea summit's ferry crossing and stage it as a maritime accident, erasing both delegates and the last witnesses to LANTERN. As Dominic's missing hours prove to be engineered memory suppression, he must choose between protecting Ilse, whom he is beginning to love and who may be the operation's inside asset, and stopping the attack; in the end he exposes the plot publicly at the summit itself, sacrificing his final alias and accepting arrest, while Ilse — revealed as the handler sent to retrieve him who instead defected — disappears with the proof that could one day clear him.
about_author: Sebastian Nystrom is a former maritime logistics consultant who spent a decade working ports from Helsinki to Gdansk before turning to fiction full-time. He writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped between institutions and their own pasts, and lives off-grid on the Swedish coast.

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. We meet him in Rotterdam under his fourth identity, running a freight brokerage, sleeping two hours a night, haunted by a gap in his memory of a night in Tallinn three years ago. A routine audit notice arrives with a phrase only LANTERN insiders would know. Emotional beat: dread resurfacing after years of numbness.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A stranger, Ilse Brandt, intercepts him at the docks and repays a favor — pulling him out of an ambush by men claiming to be port security — for something he supposedly did for her in Tallinn. He has no record of it. Emotional beat: vertigo; his careful architecture of aliases begins cracking.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. She reviews her own encrypted file: her mission was to extract Voss, not save him twice. She conceals this from him while steering them toward a safehouse. Flashbacks hint she knew him before either admits it. Emotional beat: guilt braided with reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: The Ferry Manifest
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Decoding the audit notice, they find a falsified cargo manifest aboard the Meridian Star, the chartered ferry that will carry summit delegates across the Baltic in eleven days. The 'accident' is already being staged on paper. Emotional beat: cold clarity — purpose returning like an old reflex.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. They travel to Tallinn to reconstruct Dominic's erased night. A retired harbor master recognizes him and describes behavior Dominic cannot remember: meeting someone, handing over a drive. Emotional beat: grief for a self he can't access.

chapters.title: LANTERN
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In a decommissioned signal station, they find evidence the program he exposed didn't die — it was rebranded, and its memory-suppression protocol was tested on him the night of the incident. His amnesia is not trauma; it's a product demo. Emotional beat: violation and fury.

chapters.title: Two Truths About Ilse
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic discovers a second passport for Ilse in a name tied to LANTERN's parent contractor. Confronted, she gives him half the truth: she was sent to find him, but went dark when she learned what the summit operation really was. Emotional beat: betrayal and the stubborn refusal to stop trusting her.

chapters.title: The Quiet Man in Gdansk
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. They meet Arno Kettler, the analyst who built LANTERN's memory protocol, now hiding in plain sight as a marine surveyor. He confirms the ferry attack will be blamed on a lithium battery fire — plausible, deniable, untraceable. Emotional beat: the horror of competence in service of cruelty.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Countdown structure. They map the ferry's systems and identify the saboteur's access point: a maintenance contractor with ties to the fourth name Dominic once used. Someone is wearing his old life like a coat. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Sleep, Finally
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. In a safehouse outside Kaliningrad's shadow, Dominic sleeps through the night for the first time in three years — beside Ilse. Quiet chapter: confessions, the Tallinn night partially surfacing in dream fragments, a plan forming. Emotional beat: love arriving exactly when it is most dangerous.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was Voss
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The impostor using Dominic's third alias contacts him directly: Elias Rook, a LANTERN loyalist who believes Dominic stole the drive in Tallinn. He offers Dominic reinstatement and his memories back — for silence. Emotional beat: temptation of wholeness at the price of complicity.

chapters.title: Interrogation of One
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse interrogates a captured contractor and learns the attack requires a manual override during the crossing — meaning someone aboard the ferry, likely a delegate's aide. She also learns her own handler has flagged her as compromised. Emotional beat: running out of sides to stand on.

chapters.title: Drive, Recovered
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Following the harbor master's account, they recover the Tallinn drive from a dead-drop locker. It contains the full LANTERN ledger — including the summit operation's authorization signature: a serving minister. Emotional beat: vindication curdling into despair at how high it goes.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Under stress, Dominic's suppressed memories break through violently: he remembers Ilse was in Tallinn that night — not as his rescuer, but as the technician who administered the suppression. He walks out on her. Emotional beat: heartbreak weaponized against hope.

chapters.title: What I Did That Night
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse's confession chapter. She was ordered to erase him; instead she altered the protocol, leaving a door open in his mind — the dreams, the phrase in the audit, all her doing. She chose him over the mission then, and has been paying for it since. Emotional beat: raw, unguarded love against duty.

chapters.title: Boarding
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Day of the summit crossing. Using forged crew credentials, Dominic boards the Meridian Star as a purser's assistant; Ilse works the terminal end to intercept the override signal. Rook is aboard. Emotional beat: controlled terror, the calm before.

chapters.title: Eighteen Minutes
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Real-time thriller sequence. Dominic finds the incendiary rig in the vehicle deck but triggers a lockdown; Rook corners him and offers the memory restoration one last time as the ship steams toward open water. Emotional beat: everything narrowing to a single choice.

chapters.title: The Deep Border
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Climax. Dominic refuses, fights Rook in the flooding lower deck, and broadcasts the LANTERN ledger to every newsroom and delegate terminal via the ship's own network as Ilse kills the override from shore. The 'accident' dies in daylight. Emotional beat: self-immolation as salvation.

chapters.title: Debris Field
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Aftermath at sea: Rook arrested posing as a survivor, the minister resigns under pressure, and Dominic — his last alias burned by his own broadcast — surrenders voluntarily to Finnish authorities, choosing accountability over disappearance. Emotional beat: exhausted peace.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Interrogation and hearing montage. Dominic testifies under his real name for the first time in years; the memory gaps are documented as evidence of LANTERN's crimes against him. Some charges fall away; others don't. Emotional beat: dignity reclaimed through truth-telling.

chapters.title: The Debt Owed
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse, officially a ghost, watches the trial from the public gallery and then vanishes — leaving Dominic the recovered Tallinn drive's second partition: exculpatory evidence and a single line, 'Favor returned, with interest.' Emotional beat: bittersweet devotion at a distance.

chapters.title: First Light, Open Water
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Epilogue, eighteen months later. Released early, Dominic lives openly under his real name on the Baltic coast, sleeping whole nights. A postcard arrives with no signature, only coordinates and a date. He smiles, packs one bag, and goes. Emotional beat: hope earned — love waiting on the other side of duty.
